newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar edges higher but trading thin.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar edges higher but trading thin.

text.p: Nearby white sugar futures pushed gently higher in thin volume on Monday morning, supported by talk of physical offtake, traders said.
But the market had reduced liquidity due to public holidays across Europe and the absence of leading players in New York on account of this week's Sugar Dinner.
"It's New York Sugar Week so obviously a lot of the big boys are out there," said one trader.
Commission house activity was noted on spot August but apart from unexpected interest in the August 1998 contract, volume was dominated by the two nearby months.
Trading ranges were tight a maximum 80 cents.
At 1115 GMT August was up 50 cents at $318.80 and October up by the same amount at $308.30. Overall volume was 159 lots.

Talk of continued Russian offtake was cited a factor behind the firmness in London whites, which has caused both a widening in both the August/October spread and August/July arbitrage against New York.
In physical news, Syria tendered to buy 13,000 tonnes of whites sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws, with June 17 set as the final date to receive price offers.
The two amounts should be shipped between July 15 and August 15 and results will be announced on June 18.
